title: Route config migration plan — quantization_profile_ref (Quantization Profile Library)
content:
Owner: Michael Nguyen (Platform Eng — config persistence/migrations)
Reviewers/approvers: Ethan Park (Control plane), Mina Haddad (Routing), Jordan Lee (Policy determinism), Connor O’Brien (Release), Naomi Feldman (RBAC/audit)
Last updated: 2025-03-06

Context / goal
We are adding a new route config field to support the Quantization Profile Library opt-in:
- Field: quantization_profile_ref
- Behavior: default behavior must remain unchanged when the feature is off or the field is unset.
- Enablement model: explicit per-route opt-in (ADR-0137). No global tenant default in v1.

This doc is the step-by-step plan to roll out:
1) the schema + persistence migration
2) control-plane resolution + routing policy behavior
3) runtime consumption
4) Console read/write + audit history
…across environments with safe feature flags and clear rollback.

Non-goals
- No default-on enablement across all routes/models
- No production auto-tuning / auto-recommendation
- No breaking changes to existing route config serialization


What is changing (high level)
A) Route config schema
- Add optional field: quantization_profile_ref
  - Values:
    - "default" (explicitly indicates baseline; used for clarity in API/Console)
    - "profile:<profile_id>@<version>" (explicit pinned version; preferred for determinism)
    - (tentative) "alias:recommended" and "alias:latest" are NOT enabled for GA unless we add a “no silent change” guard (see Open Questions)

B) Control plane / policy engine
- Resolve quantization_profile_ref at request planning time.
- Perform compatibility checks (model variant, hardware SKU class, max context regime) and return deterministic resolution:
  - applied(profile_id)
  - fallback(baseline) with reason
  - disabled(feature off / kill switch)

C) Runtime
- Runtime reads resolved profile (if any) and loads profile artifacts.
- Emits metrics + log annotations quant_profile_id and resolution outcome.

D) Global safety controls
- Platform kill switch: disables applying any profile, irrespective of route config.
- Audit events for any route config change.


Feature flags / config knobs
We will use explicit, layered flags to avoid partial rollout failures:

1) Flag: route_config.quant_profiles_field_read_enabled
- Control plane + router can read/deserialize the new field from config store
- Default: OFF in all envs until DB migration is complete

2) Flag: route_config.quant_profiles_field_write_enabled
- Allows API/Console to write quantization_profile_ref
- Default: OFF until read path is stable and we have audit coverage

3) Flag: quant_profiles.apply_enabled
- Allows policy engine to return “applied(profile)” as an outcome
- Default: OFF until runtime is deployed everywhere and has guardrails

4) Flag: quant_profiles.kill_switch (global)
- Hard override (if ON): policy engine forces baseline outcome; runtime ignores any resolved profile
- Default: OFF
- SRE can flip without deploy

5) Allowlist (beta only): quant_profiles.route_allowlist
- Routes allowed to enable profile application (even if apply_enabled is ON)
- Default: empty
- Removed/relaxed at GA when we are comfortable (decision TBD)


Environments and rollout order
Environments:
- dev
- staging
- perf-canary
- prod

Rollout order by component:
1) Config store + migrations (Platform Eng)
2) Control plane read path + policy evaluation (Control plane + Routing)
3) Runtime consumption + metrics (Serving runtime)
4) Console (backend + UI) + RBAC + audit (Console/tooling)
5) Gradual enablement flags + allowlists (Release/SRE)


Data model + migration details
Current state:
- Route config records stored in <route_config_store> (DB table + cached layer) with JSON blob for config fields.
- Multiple services deserialize the route config; some are strict.

Migration goals:
- Backward compatible read: old services ignore the new field (or don’t see it) until deployed.
- Backward compatible write: do not write new field until all strict deserializers are deployed.

Planned approach
Phase M0: Pre-flight compatibility audit (DONE / in progress)
- Inventory all consumers of route config serialization.
- Identify any strict JSON parsing or schema validation that would break on unknown field.
- Owners:
  - Michael Nguyen to provide list
  - Mina Haddad + Jordan Lee to confirm router/policy parsing behavior

Phase M1: Add nullable column OR JSON field support (depending on store)
- If we store route config as JSON blob, no DB schema change is needed, but we need to update validators and migration tooling.
- If there is a typed schema table for critical fields, add nullable column quantization_profile_ref.
- Implement “read support” in the persistence layer first.
- Deliverable: safe to read new field if present; still not written by any client.

Phase M2: Online migration (no-op for existing routes)
- Ensure existing routes default to implicit baseline behavior.
- Do not backfill any value.
- Add tooling validation that missing field == baseline.

Phase M3: Enable read flag
- Flip route_config.quant_profiles_field_read_enabled in dev -> staging -> perf-canary -> prod.
- Verify all services correctly ignore/handle absent field.

Phase M4: Enable write in non-prod
- Flip route_config.quant_profiles_field_write_enabled in dev/staging.
- Only allow “default” value at first to test write path + audit.
- Then allow pinned profile ref behind allowlist.


Rollout stages (end-to-end)
Stage 0 — Code deployed, flags OFF everywhere
Target: no behavior change
Prereqs:
- PRs merged and deployed:
  - Route config field + migration tooling (pr-18411, pr-18605)
  - Kill switch plumbing (pr-18488)
  - Policy compatibility checks (pr-18427)
  - Runtime metrics + log annotation (pr-18463, pr-18555)
  - Control plane API endpoints + audit events (pr-18445, pr-18503)

Checks:
- Synthetic tests confirm baseline behavior unchanged when field absent.
- Integration test: route config deserialization across services with unknown field (where applicable).

Stage 1 — Enable READ in dev/staging
Flags:
- route_config.quant_profiles_field_read_enabled = ON (dev/staging)
- write_enabled = OFF
- apply_enabled = OFF

What we expect:
- Nothing applies; no change to runtime.
- We can confirm services can load configs that include quantization_profile_ref (even though none exist yet).

Validation:
- Create a route config record with quantization_profile_ref manually in dev (DB console) and ensure no crashes.
- Router/policy returns “disabled(feature off)” outcome if it sees field.

Stage 2 — Enable WRITE in dev/staging (baseline-only)
Flags:
- read_enabled = ON
- write_enabled = ON
- apply_enabled = OFF

Constraints:
- API/Console only accept quantization_profile_ref = "default" for this stage.
- Ensure audit events emit correctly (actor, route_id, diff includes quantization_profile_ref).

Validation:
- Console can write/clear the value and show change history.
- Exported audit logs include quant_profile_id field (even if blank) per INT-9170 request.

Stage 3 — perf-canary end-to-end with apply still OFF
Flags:
- read_enabled = ON (perf-canary)
- write_enabled = ON (perf-canary)
- apply_enabled = OFF

Goal:
- Validate high-QPS config caching + registry fetch protection before we apply anything.
- Confirm no thundering herd on metadata fetch endpoints.

Validation:
- Load test: high QPS with config reads; ensure cache hit rate stable.
- Ensure any profile metadata fetches are rate-limited/cached (pr-18547).

Stage 4 — perf-canary apply ON for allowlisted route(s)
Flags:
- read_enabled = ON
- write_enabled = ON
- apply_enabled = ON (perf-canary)
- route_allowlist includes 1–2 perf-canary routes
- kill_switch = OFF

Execution:
- Create a perf-canary route with pinned profile ref (profile:<id>@<version>) for a supported model.
- Monitor:
  - fallback_rate
  - applied_rate
  - p95 decode latency / TTFT
  - 5xx
  - runtime “profile loaded” errors

Success criteria (for this stage):
- fallback_rate < 1% (excluding intentional incompat tests)
- no 5xx increase
- p95 latency within agreed threshold from perf suite

Stage 5 — Production: READ ON (no write/apply)
Flags:
- read_enabled = ON (prod)
- write_enabled = OFF (prod)
- apply_enabled = OFF (prod)

Goal:
- Ensure production services tolerate the new field if it appears (e.g., from config replication or future writes).

Stage 6 — Production: WRITE ON for allowlisted users/routes (still apply OFF)
Flags:
- write_enabled = ON (prod)
- apply_enabled = OFF
- RBAC gating: only org admins / platform role can set field

Goal:
- Allow design partner(s) to pre-configure the field, visible in Console, with zero runtime effect.

Stage 7 — Production: APPLY ON for allowlisted routes
Flags:
- apply_enabled = ON (prod)
- route_allowlist = design partner route IDs only
- kill_switch = OFF

Rollout steps:
- Start with 0.5–1% traffic for 1 route (if traffic splitting is supported at routing layer), otherwise start with a low-traffic route.
- Expand to additional routes/models after 24h stable.

Stop/rollback triggers:
- fallback_rate spike > agreed threshold (SRE to define exact number; draft: sustained >5% for 10 min)
- 5xx increase correlated with profile application
- p95 latency regression beyond SLO budget
- Quality guardrail alert (from eval harness / online monitors)


Operational rollback plan
Goal: restore baseline behavior quickly without requiring a deploy.

Rollback lever hierarchy (fastest to slowest)
1) Per-route disable (preferred)
- Set quantization_profile_ref = "default" or clear field
- Expected propagation: config cache TTL + push interval (document current TTL; target < 2 minutes)
- Use when: single route or single tenant issue

2) Remove route from allowlist
- If issue is contained but route config churn is high
- Keep apply_enabled ON for other routes

3) Global kill switch
- quant_profiles.kill_switch = ON
- Forces baseline outcomes for all routes regardless of config
- Use when: widespread regression / unknown scope / incident response

4) Flip apply_enabled OFF
- Disables application but still allows reading/writing fields
- Use when: we want to pause rollout but keep configuration state

5) (Last resort) revert write_enabled
- Prevents further changes; existing configs remain
- Not typically needed for performance/quality rollback

Verification after rollback
- Confirm applied_rate drops to 0 and fallback/disabled outcome dominates
- Confirm p95/p99 latency and 5xx return to baseline
- Confirm runtime logs show resolution outcome “disabled(kill_switch)” or “baseline”


Risk register (migration-specific)
1) Strict deserialization failure in a legacy service
- Mitigation: Stage 0 inventory + Stage 1 read-only rollout; canary deploy to perf-canary before prod read

2) Partial rollout causes inconsistent behavior across clusters
- Mitigation: apply_enabled requires runtime version gate; do not flip apply_enabled until runtime deployed everywhere

3) Thundering herd on model registry/profile metadata
- Mitigation: caching + rate limiting (pr-18547), plus Stage 3 perf-canary stress

4) Silent profile change via alias semantics
- Mitigation: v1 prefers pinned profile IDs. Aliases deferred unless we add explicit “customer ack” semantics.


Runbook snippets (for release/oncall)
Finding whether a request used a profile:
- Look up request_id trace/log
- Check fields:
  - quant_profile_id
  - quant_profile_resolution_outcome (applied|fallback|disabled)
  - fallback_reason (if present)

If customer reports output differences:
- Confirm route config value
- Compare applied_rate/fallback_rate
- Suggest A/B eval via eval harness playbook before re-enabling


Open questions
1) Do we allow alias:recommended / alias:latest in GA?
- Concern: silent change without explicit customer action; also complicates determinism.
- Proposed: keep aliases internal-only for beta; GA supports only pinned profile refs + “default”.

2) Backfill "default" value or leave unset?
- Leaving unset is simplest and preserves historical behavior.
- Console UX may prefer explicit “default”; can treat unset as default in UI without writing.

3) Propagation SLO for route config changes
- Need exact numbers for cache TTL and publish interval for rollback expectations.


Appendix A — Checklist for each environment
Dev
- [ ] Deploy latest control plane + router + runtime builds
- [ ] read_enabled ON
- [ ] Validate manual config with field does not crash

Staging
- [ ] read_enabled ON
- [ ] write_enabled ON (default-only)
- [ ] Confirm audit events in staging SIEM sink

Perf-canary
- [ ] Stress test config + metadata fetch
- [ ] apply_enabled ON for allowlisted route
- [ ] Confirm dashboard panels exist (enabled/applied/fallback)

Prod
- [ ] read_enabled ON (24h)
- [ ] write_enabled ON for allowlisted admins
- [ ] apply_enabled ON for allowlisted routes only
- [ ] Kill switch verified functional (dry run in prod with no routes allowlisted)


Appendix B — Related docs
- ADR-0137 Route-level quantization profile enablement
- Confluence: quantization profile compatibility and fallbacks
- Confluence: quantization profile config service
- Runbook: rollback procedure — quantization profiles
